//: Who may touch what, written down BEFORE anyone starts. Read docs/parallel-dev.md first, then BOTH briefs: docs/specs/unipile-rooms-and-booking.md and docs/specs/adgrant-and-dev-agents.md. THIS IS PROGRAMME THREE, second half. Its first five parcels are landed and are kept in docs/parcels-programme-3-landed.json; programme two's thirteen are in docs/parcels-programme-2.json and programme one's nineteen in docs/parcels-programme-1.json. None of those three files is for running. Ownership freed by a retired parcel is reused here on purpose: adgrant-site inherits the AdGrant tree from adgrant-front, and booking-picker inherits the dialog from booking-dialog.
//brief: Two briefs, and a parcel reads the one its prompt names. unipile-rooms-and-booking.md carries the Unipile contract, the identity decisions and the rule that every inbound message is checked for who it is from, who it is to and which chat it is in. adgrant-and-dev-agents.md carries adgrant.ai's own content API, the six factual defects in the material being carried over, the split between generating a structure and uploading it, and the answer to the owner's question about per-agent limits. An agent that starts from a paraphrase instead will rebuild something that already exists or ship something that is wrong.
//seams: Files everything needs. A parcel may ADD up to three lines to one of these and delete none, and must declare which lines up front. Two one-line additions merge by keeping both; two thirty-line edits merge into something nobody can verify. THREE STATED EXCEPTIONS, carried over because the three-line grammar would make them unusable: scripts/build-kb.ts admits one appended Corpus const plus its name on the CORPORA line, shared/roster.ts admits one whole appended agent entry, and client/src/components/site/doors/bodies.tsx admits one door-to-body entry. All three are appends at the end of a list, which is the shape that merges. A FOURTH, added for programme three: shared/schema.ts admits one re-export line. A new table is fifteen lines and the seam allows three, so a parcel that needs a table writes it in its OWN file and re-exports it from the schema - drizzle-kit follows the export, and one line merges where fifteen do not.
//frozen: Nobody edits these during a parallel run. A change here invalidates every parcel at once. Programme three has one consequence worth stating: client/index.html carries the one <head> this application serves, so a second site on a second host cannot have its own title and meta without editing a frozen file. That is why adgrant-front builds a route tree and not a second host - the host switch is owner work, done when no wave is running.
//alone: Parcels marked runAlone touch the room, the panel or the shell - everything reads those, and two agents in them at once produce a merge nobody can check. One agent, let it finish, then start the others.
//order: The waves are in scripts/build-prompts.mjs and check-parcels.mjs reads them back. Programme three's ordering is a dependency chain, not a preference, and it has three links. (1) unipile-core is wave one ALONE because four parcels import its client; a parcel that writes its own Unipile client because the shared one did not exist yet is four incompatible error mappers. (2) booking-server and booking-dialog are the same wave and build to the request and response shapes fixed in the brief's section 3 - that is what fixing them in writing was for. (3) room-identity precedes login-create-room, because the claim dialog the site's new menu opens is the one room-identity builds. Beyond the chain, one standing rule: AT MOST ONE PARCEL PER WAVE MAY TOUCH server/routes.ts. Three parcels here need a route, and they are in three different waves for that reason alone.

server/routes.ts: the routes that show, change and cancel a booking
shared/api.ts: what the popup learns about a booking already made
shared/schema.ts: one re-export line if a booking becomes a row

booking-return.why: The owner booked through the QR code and it worked, and then everything after it was missing. Pressing Book a call again offers an empty picker as though nothing happened; there is no way to change the time and no way to cancel; and somebody who booked from a phone and closed the tab has no way back to the booking at all. A booking a person cannot get out of is a booking they will simply not attend, and the calendar keeps the slot.
booking-return.done: A BOOKING YOU CAN COME BACK TO, CHANGE, AND CANCEL. Read docs/review/next-waves.md, section booking-return — it is the owner's own words and it is the specification. (1) THE BROWSER REMEMBERS. A successful booking is recorded in the site's own session, and pressing Book a call again opens the confirmation rather than the picker. THAT FLAG IS A POINTER, NOT A CREDENTIAL: on its own it must never be enough to read or change a booking, because a cookie is copyable and a booking carries somebody's name, time and address. The server decides what may be shown, every time. (2) TWO LINKS IN THE CONFIRMATION: change, and cancel. (3) A WAY BACK FROM ANYWHERE for a WhatsApp booking — a short address the owner writes as https://top-rated.team/<code> that opens the site with that booking's popup already open. The code IS the credential there, so treat it as one: it expires with the booking, it is single-purpose, and it is never logged. Decide deliberately whether a bare /<code> at the site root can collide with any existing route, and say what you decided. (4) CLEARING IT. Cancelling clears the flag; so does the call time passing. Neither can be relied on — the flag is per browser and a person may cancel from another device — so the SERVER's answer decides what the popup shows and the flag is only a hint about what to ask for. (5) CANCELLING DELETES THE EVENT. Where there is an address, let Google tell them. Where the booking was proved by WhatsApp, the message goes to the chat that proved it and nowhere else, and never to a chat that did not. (6) CHANGING IS A CANCEL AND A BOOK, in that order, and the new slot is re-checked as free before the old one is released — losing somebody's slot while moving it is worse than refusing the move.

server/routes.ts: the session routes: who am I, and sign out
shared/api.ts: what the control learns about whoever is signed in
shared/schema.ts: one re-export line for the account and session tables

room-account.why: The control says Login in every state, because there is no state to read. Wave 13's sign-in is stateless: you prove who you are, the server answers with the rooms bound to that identity, you pick one, and what remembers you afterwards is a room token in localStorage. There is no session, so there is nothing for a Logout to end and nothing for a second way in to be attached to. The owner has asked for both.
room-account.done: AN ACCOUNT, A SESSION, AND THE THREE THINGS THAT FOLLOW. Read docs/review/next-waves.md, section room-account — it is the owner's own design. (1) A DURABLE IDENTITY with a cookie that points at it. The cookie is a credential: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite, rotated on sign-in, and LONG — the owner's instruction is to remember somebody for as long as possible, so an expiry measured in days is wrong. (2) THE LABEL IS STATE AND MUST BE READ FROM THE SERVER, never from a localStorage flag. A page that says Logout to somebody with no session, or Login to somebody who has one, is worse than one that says neither, and a cookie is not readable from JavaScript if it is HttpOnly — which it must be. One small endpoint that answers who, if anyone, this is. (3) LOGOUT ENDS THE SESSION AND NOTHING ELSE. It must NOT forget the rooms in localStorage: signing out of a shared browser and losing your own rooms on your own laptop would be one word doing two jobs, and the owner's standing rule is to remember a visitor as long as possible. (4) HOVERING LOGOUT OFFERS THE OTHER WAYS IN, so a person signed in by email can attach LinkedIn, or WhatsApp on a house host, and the rooms already bound to that other identity become reachable from this account. THE MERGE IS THE DANGEROUS OPERATION IN THIS WHOLE PARCEL: decide what happens when the second identity already belongs to another account, and REFUSE rather than guess — silently joining two accounts hands one person's rooms to another, and a room token is a bearer credential. Write that branch's test first. WHAT MUST NOT CHANGE: the pair is Login | Open a room and Logout | Open a room — one pair in every state — and each half keeps its own hover, rooms under 'Open a room' and ways in under the left half. WhatsApp stays house-only, for the reason shared/operator.ts exists. A fork with no LinkedIn app and no mail configured must still render a control that says something true rather than an empty panel.

server/routes.ts: the two routes that connect and drop a visitor's calendar
shared/api.ts: what the picker learns about a connected calendar

visitor-calendar.why: The owner has asked for this four times and it has never existed. It was designed, he published a Google Cloud app for it with the non-sensitive calendar.freebusy scope, and then no parcel ever built it — while /privacy described it in the present tense until that was found and corrected. It is also what blocks the demo video Google's verification wants, because there is no flow to record.
visitor-calendar.done: A VISITOR CAN CONNECT THEIR OWN GOOGLE CALENDAR SO WE DO NOT OFFER THEM A TIME THEY ARE ALREADY BUSY. Read docs/review/next-waves.md, section visitor-calendar, first. IT NEEDS TWO VALUES THAT ARE NOT IN THE REPOSITORY: the client id and secret of the owner's separate Google Cloud app — separate from the scheduling connector's, which is OURS and stays. Read them from GOOGLE_FREEBUSY_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_FREEBUSY_CLIENT_SECRET, document both in .env.example, and BE COMPLETELY INERT WITHOUT THEM: the picker shows no such option and says nothing about one. (1) THE SCOPE IS calendar.freebusy AND NOTHING ELSE. It is non-sensitive precisely because freeBusy.query returns busy intervals — no titles, no guests, no locations, no descriptions — and asking for one field more turns a light consent screen into a Google security review. (2) IT IS THE VISITOR'S GOOGLE, NOT OURS. Two apps, two consent screens. The visitor's token is held for the length of the booking and never written down: not to the database, not to a log, not to a session store that outlives the pick. The connection ends when they confirm or after five minutes, whichever comes first. (3) DISCONNECTING REMOVES THAT VISITOR'S OWN GOOGLE ACCOUNT AND NOTHING ELSE — never dan@top-rated.team, never any LinkedIn or WhatsApp account. The owner said so in those words. (4) BUSY MEANS OFFERED-AS-BUSY, NOT HIDDEN: a slot the visitor is busy in is marked, not removed, because a person may still choose it, and silently shrinking the list makes the picker look broken. (5) THE PRIVACY PAGE MOVES BACK TO THE PRESENT TENSE IN THE SAME COMMIT, not before and not after. Its row currently says, correctly, that this is not built; that row is part of this parcel and it is the last thing to change. (6) A FORK HAS NO SUCH APP, so this is off there by default and the picker never mentions it. WHAT MUST NOT CHANGE: our own calendar is still read through the scheduling connector, and the slot list is still computed the way server/booking/slots.ts computes it today — this ADDS a second, optional overlay from the visitor's side, it does not replace the first.
